name: NIST SP 800-171
full_name: NIST Special Publication 800-171 Revision 2, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations
NIST SP 800-171A, Assessing Security Requirements for Controlled Unclassified Information (June 2018)
NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Methodology, Version 1.2.1 (June 24, 2020)
32 CFR Part 170, Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Program
sources.publisher: eCFR, Office of the Federal Register

scoring.summary: Start at 110 and subtract each unimplemented requirement's point value (DoD Assessment Methodology). The score can be negative.

rules.summary: A requirement is implemented only when every assessment objective is satisfied.
The score of 110 is reduced by each requirement not implemented and may be negative.
rules.quote: The score of 110 is reduced by each requirement not implemented, which may result in a negative score.

3.5.3.partial_label: MFA implemented for remote and privileged users only

rules.summary: 3.5.3 and 3.13.11 subtract 3 points when partially implemented and 5 when not implemented.
rules.quote: If encryption is employed, but is not FIPS validated, 3 points are subtracted from the score of 110.

rules.summary: A system security plan must exist; it carries no point value, and without it the assessment cannot be completed.
rules.quote: The contractor must have a system security plan (Basic Security Requirement 3.12.4) in place

rules.summary: A requirement not yet implemented is still scored as not implemented while it is on a plan of action; a plan of action earns no points.
rules.quote: Security requirements not implemented, whether a plan of action is in place or not, will be assessed as 'not implemented.

rules.summary: Assessments are expected every three years unless risk or change drives a different frequency.
rules.quote: is anticipated to be once every three years unless other factors

consequences.summary: Contractors handling CUI under DFARS 252.204-7012 must post a current score to SPRS; a low or missing score can affect contract eligibility.
consequences.quote: Date a score of 110 is expected to be achieved

glossary.definition: Controlled Unclassified Information: government information that is not classified but must still be protected.
Federal Contract Information: information provided by or generated for the government under a contract and not intended for public release.
Supplier Performance Risk System, where contractors record assessment scores and affirmations.
Plan of Action and Milestones: the documented plan for closing requirements that are not yet met.
System Security Plan: the document that describes the system in scope and how each requirement is implemented.
Federal Information Processing Standards; FIPS 140 validation confirms a cryptographic module has been independently tested.
Multi-factor authentication: signing in with two or more independent factors.
National Institute of Standards and Technology, the U.S. agency that publishes the 800-171 requirements.
